summary: The paper presents a source-level polyhedral framework that turns sequential affine loop nests into MPI code without any programmer-supplied data distribution. Per-tile flow-out and write-out sets are computed at compile time, and run-time helper functions find the receiving processes, so each needed element is sent only to the processes that read it.
why_read: It is a concrete, end-to-end account of how a polyhedral compiler can generate correct MPI communication code for arbitrary affine loop nests.
main_contribution: Parametric communication code generation for affine loop nests, valid for any process count and any affine computation partition.
main_limitation: Every process holds all data, and communication volume is not optimal when parts of one flow-out set have different receivers.
evaluation_method: Strong scaling on a 32-node InfiniBand cluster, compared with sequential code, Pluto-sequential code, hand-written MPI, a naive all-gather variant and pghpf.
